author: w. a. orozco
title: Nancy Mace highlights animal welfare measure and addresses safety concerns in recent posts - Berkeley Leader
text:
U.S. Representative Nancy Mace, who has represented South Carolina’s 1st district in Congress since 2021, addressed a range of issues in a series of posts on October 15, 2025. Mace, who previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives and is a graduate of The Citadel, used her social media platform to highlight legislative developments and comment on recent events.
In one post on October 15, 2025, Mace announced the passage of a provision related to animal welfare: “MACE WIN: We secured a provision in the House-passed NDAA to prohibit the cruel experiments on dogs and cats in Department of War labs passed the House. For too long, taxpayer dollars have funded painful experiments on animals, and in some cases, those funds have even gone to https://t.co/YqjAeICxNV”.
Later that day, she expressed support for survivors and commented on recent legal proceedings: “To every survivor who’s been ignored or attacked for speaking up, you are not alone. The courts saw through the lies and the lawfare. The truth will always rise. HOLD THE LINE. https://t.co/xgvWLoP5If”.
Mace also acknowledged an emergency landing involving Secretary Hegseth and his team: “We are relieved Secretary Hegseth and his team are safe after today’s emergency landing. God bless the pilots, crew, and individuals who keep our defense leaders secure at home and abroad. “.
Nancy Mace has been an active figure in Congress since succeeding Joe Cunningham in 2021. She was born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977 and currently resides in Charleston. Before her tenure in Congress, she served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020 and earned her undergraduate degree from The Citadel in 1999.
